text: I'll start with the StatefulSet and its PVC.

arguments.root_cause_statement: The StatefulSet analytics/metrics-db declares a volumeClaimTemplate named "data" whose storageClassName is "fast-ssd". No StorageClass by that name exists in this cluster; the only StorageClass present is "standard" (rancher.io/local-path), which is also the default. The PersistentVolumeClaim data-metrics-db-0 that the StatefulSet controller created from that template therefore stays Pending with "storageclass.storage.k8s.io \"fast-ssd\" not found", pod metrics-db-0 cannot be scheduled because its claim is unbound, and the StatefulSet stays at 0/1 Ready — which is why the Service metrics-db has no endpoint addresses and the dashboards are empty. Correct the volumeClaimTemplate to storageClassName "standard" (or omit it to take the default); because volumeClaimTemplates are immutable, the StatefulSet must be recreated (kubectl delete statefulset metrics-db --cascade=orphan) and the stale Pending PVC data-metrics-db-0 deleted so it is recreated against the valid class.
arguments.mechanism: The StatefulSet analytics/metrics-db sets .spec.volumeClaimTemplates[0].spec.storageClassName to "fast-ssd", a StorageClass that does not exist in the cluster (the only one is "standard"), so the PersistentVolumeClaim data-metrics-db-0 it generates is rejected by the persistentvolume-controller with "storageclass.storage.k8s.io \"fast-ssd\" not found" and stays Pending. With that claim unbound, the scheduler rejects pod metrics-db-0 ("pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims"), so the StatefulSet is stuck reporting 0/1 Ready.

evidence.claim: The paged StatefulSet reports 0/1 ready and its only pod is Pending and unscheduled.
The StatefulSet's volumeClaimTemplate asks for StorageClass fast-ssd.
evidence.quote:
Volume Claims:
  Name:          data
  StorageClass:  fast-ssd

evidence.claim: The generated PVC carries storageClassName fast-ssd.
Provisioning of that PVC fails because the named StorageClass does not exist, leaving the PVC Pending.
evidence.quote: Warning  ProvisioningFailed  1s (x2 over 1s)  persistentvolume-controller  storageclass.storage.k8s.io "fast-ssd" not found

evidence.claim: The only StorageClass in the cluster is standard, which is the default.
The unbound claim is the reason the pod cannot be scheduled.
evidence.quote: Warning  FailedScheduling  0s    default-scheduler  0/1 nodes are available: pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims. not found

ruled_out.alternative: Node capacity, taints or node pressure prevented scheduling.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The single node is Ready with full allocatable CPU, memory and 110 pod slots, and the scheduler's stated reason is the unbound claim, not resources or taints.
ruled_out.quote:
node/incident-lab-control-plane cpu=6/6 memory=12220316Ki/12220316Ki pods=110 (capacity/allocatable)
  condition Ready=True

ruled_out.alternative: The Service selector does not match the pod labels, so endpoints are empty for a labelling reason.
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The Service selector app=metrics-db matches the pod template labels exactly; the endpoint list is empty only because no pod is running.

ruled_out.alternative: The container image or command is broken (bad image pull, crash loop).
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod never reached a node at all — it has no node assigned and PodScheduled is False — so no container was ever started or pulled.
